concepts.definition: Work performed primarily away from an employer or customer site, with remote work explicitly available.
Work explicitly described as fully remote, remote-only, or 100 percent remote.
A recurring mix of remote work and scheduled work at an office, facility, or customer site.
Work that requires regular physical presence at an office, facility, installation, or customer site.
Occasional or limited work travel, generally no more than about 10 percent.
Recurring moderate work travel, generally around 11 to 25 percent.
Frequent or extensive work travel, generally more than 50 percent.
Substantial work travel, generally around 26 to 50 percent.
Temporary deployment away from the normal work location to support operations, projects, or customer missions.
An assignment requiring extended periods away from home or the normal duty location.
A requirement or explicit expectation that the candidate relocate for the role.
A recurring rotational work schedule that alternates blocks of duty and time away.
A role or assignment requiring work in another country or an OCONUS location.
Hands-on or operational work inside data-center environments.
Hands-on interaction with racks, equipment, cabling, power, or facilities systems.
Work regularly performed in engineering, research, test, or hardware laboratories.
Work performed in production, assembly, or manufacturing environments.
Work around aircraft, hangars, ramps, or flight-line operations.
Routine work inside secure classified facilities with access or device restrictions.
Routine work performed at customer-controlled facilities rather than your normal office or home.
Regular work outdoors at operational, test, construction, or equipment sites.
Work aboard ships or vessels, potentially including time underway.
Work requiring underwater or diving activities.
Work requiring entry into restricted spaces such as tanks, shafts, or crawlspaces.
Work requiring ladders, lifts, towers, rooftops, or elevated platforms.
Engineering work performed at operational, customer, or equipment sites.
Primarily responsible for direct technical work rather than managing people.
Designing, implementing, testing, and maintaining software systems.
Requirements, architecture, integration, interfaces, verification, and whole-system behavior.
CI/CD, developer platforms, infrastructure automation, and operational tooling.
Designing and operating cloud infrastructure, services, and platforms.
Building, integrating, or operationalizing machine-learning and AI systems.
Building data pipelines, storage, transformation, and data-platform systems.
Statistical analysis, experimentation, predictive modeling, and analytical modeling.
Security engineering, analysis, architecture, or other cybersecurity work.
Network architecture, routing, switching, connectivity, and related systems.
Systems, servers, virtualization, storage, operating platforms, and related infrastructure.
Hands-on technical work performed at customer, equipment, or operational sites.
Verification, validation, test design, automation, and proving systems meet requirements.
Coordinating broad programs, budgets, schedules, stakeholders, and delivery across projects.
Planning and coordinating defined projects, schedules, resources, risks, and deliverables.
Formal responsibility for employees, staffing, performance, development, or hiring.
Design, integration, testing, or support of hardware and physical electronic systems.
Hands-on maintenance, repair, servicing, and mechanical troubleshooting of vehicles, machinery, equipment, or physical systems.
Producing, assembling, machining, welding, or fabricating physical parts, structures, equipment, or assemblies.
Hands-on inspection, acceptance, and quality-control verification of physical equipment, parts, installations, materials, or workmanship.
Technician-level hands-on setup, instrumentation, measurement, test execution, and laboratory support.
Physical receiving, stocking, picking, shipping, inventory movement, warehouse operations, and material handling.
Direct plant-floor production, assembly-line, manufacturing, or production-equipment operations.
A large portion of the job is coordination, planning, or management rather than direct technical execution.
Significant direct building, coding, configuring, testing, or troubleshooting.
Significant responsibility for architecture, design direction, interfaces, and technical decisions.
Regular direct interaction with customers, stakeholders, or external users.
Leading a technical team without necessarily having formal personnel authority.
Formal employee responsibility including hiring, reviews, staffing, or development.
Accountability for budgets, cost performance, or financial planning.
Accountability for schedules, milestones, dependencies, or delivery performance.
Business-development work involving proposals, bids, capture strategy, or winning new work.
A substantial portion of the role involves formal documentation or compliance artifacts.
Ongoing support, maintenance, monitoring, incident response, or lifecycle sustainment.
Investigation, experimentation, prototyping, or evaluation of new techniques.
Building user-facing or business-facing applications.
Server-side services, business logic, databases, and APIs.
Client-side application interfaces and user-facing web or UI development.
Designing and implementing programmatic service interfaces.
Automating workflows, operations, or repetitive tasks with scripts or tooling.
Administration, configuration, maintenance, and troubleshooting of Linux systems.
Administration, configuration, maintenance, and troubleshooting of Windows systems.
Containerization, orchestration, Docker, Kubernetes, and related platforms.
Declarative infrastructure using tools such as Terraform or CloudFormation.
Network architecture, routing, switching, connectivity, and related technologies.
Cisco-specific networking technologies, platforms, and tooling.
Storage systems, platforms, capacity, performance, and related administration.
Virtual machines, hypervisors, virtual infrastructure, and related platforms.
Electrical power, cooling, facilities, or other physical infrastructure systems.
Physical installation, cabling, rack-mounted equipment, and related infrastructure work.
Software and systems running on embedded or device-level hardware.
Statistical or learned models trained from data.
Broad AI systems, techniques, and AI-enabled capabilities.
Processing, understanding, or generating human language.
Transformer and LLM-based systems for language understanding, generation, or reasoning.
General implementation and maintenance of software systems.
Developing or operating in Linux environments.
AWS, Azure, GCP, and related cloud-native services.
Automated build, test, release, and deployment pipelines.
